terms.title: The Shattered Crown
terms.guideSubtitle: Sword and sorcery for the Legend Dynamics RPG system
terms.journalIntro: Write it together at the end of a venture. Advancements apply to the GM's copies; use each card's Save character file to send a player their update.
terms.journalTitlePlaceholder: e.g. The Tomb of the Serpent Kings
terms.reload: Reload (crossbow: an action; firearm: a full round)
terms.reloadDone: Reloaded. A crossbow took your action; a firearm took the whole round.
terms.restockDone: Restocked in town: quiver, bolts and powder full.
terms.emptyNote: Empty: reload before you can loose or fire again.
terms.tracksIntro: Shared by the whole party. Killing in the open, blatant sorcery, buying on credit or days in the wilds without supplies can mark a box. Lying low, a cleansing rite, paying up or reaching a town can clear one.
terms.facility: A temple infirmary or a master healer's house
terms.formCoreSummary: Beast form: changing takes an action; fury or the scent of blood can force it (Will roll); its profile applies while changed; you can't speak, cast or use tools
terms.restrictedToggle: Dark campaign: show the Undying as player characters (they drain the living; only if the whole table agreed)
terms.restrictedCheck: for dark campaigns only: tick Dark campaign if your table agreed
terms.titlePlaceholder: e.g. Reaver of the Ulfang clan

roles.name: Barbarian
roles.text: Barbarian: came out of the wild places with an axe and an appetite, and trusts strength over sorcery.

roles.name: Sellsword
roles.text: Sellsword: fights for coin and keeps the contract, mostly; knows how battles are really won.

roles.name: Duelist
roles.text: Duelist: a blade, a reputation and a quick tongue, and the grace to use all three.

roles.name: Corsair
roles.text: Corsair: sea-raider and free captain, as at home in the rigging as in a boarding fight.

roles.name: Thief
roles.text: Thief: no lock, wall or guard is enough, and the bigger the prize the better.

roles.name: Assassin
roles.text: Assassin: patient, precise, and paid in advance; studies a mark before the knife.

roles.name: Outrider
roles.text: Outrider: scouts the way, finds the water, and sees the ambush first.

roles.name: Charlatan
roles.text: Charlatan: a false prince, a fortune-teller, a forged deed; whatever the mark wants to believe.

roles.name: Sorcerer
roles.text: Sorcerer: learned the forbidden arts from books and worse teachers, and pays for every spell.

roles.name: Witch
roles.text: Witch: hedge-magic, herbs and curses, learned at a grandmother's knee or a devil's.

roles.name: Priest
roles.text: Priest: speaks for a god who may be dying, performs the old rites, and tends the wounded.

roles.name: Alchemist
roles.text: Alchemist: powders, poisons, cures and black powder; half scholar, half bomb-maker.

skills: Command, rally, inspire, keep a band together
Bargain, convince, seduce, calm a crowd
Lie, bluff, disguise, cheat at dice
Spot a lie, read intent, sense an ambush
Search a place, piece clues together, find a hidden door
History, languages, ruins, gods and monsters
Cast and resist spells, work rituals, sense magic
Bind wounds, treat poison and disease
Smithing, traps, black powder, bombs and alchemy
Pick locks and pockets, palm, disarm traps
Follow a trail, hunt, read signs
Wilderness, desert, cold, foraging and shelter
Horses, camels and war-beasts, mounted combat
Ships, rivers, weather and the sea
Climb, swim, run, leap and dodge
formCore: Takes an action, in or out, except when fury or the moon forces it.
Fury, terror or the scent of blood can force a change: when it matters, the GM calls for a Will roll.

While changed, the form's attribute bonuses apply to rolls on those attributes and their skills, even above the starting maximum; its traits and drawbacks apply too. In human form, none of it does: the sheet's form switch shows both sets of numbers.
A beast form seen in a town or camp marks a box of Infamy.

origins.name: Northlander
origins.desc: From the frozen north: clans, longships and long winters. Hard to kill and slow to forgive.
traits: +2 to Survival in cold, snow and storm.
Your clan's quarrels follow you south. Accept the old enemy who turns up.
+2 to Melee to break a shield, a door or a guard with an axe.
Walls, crowds and soft manners make you clumsy. Accept the gaffe, or the brawl.
+2 to Sailing on rivers and cold seas.
You must be the hero of the song. Accept the risk for the glory.

origins.name: Crownlander
origins.desc: Born in the Gilded Cities that were once the empire's heart: silk, intrigue, and knives in the dark.
traits: +2 to Persuasion in courts, councils and noble houses.
Your family name opens doors and old grudges. Accept the enemy it brings.
+2 to Investigation to find someone or something in a city.
Wilderness and hardship are new to you. Accept the misery or the mistake.
+2 to Lore to read old scripts, decrees and maps.
Fine wine, silk and lotus call to you. Accept the indulgence.

origins.name: Sand-born
origins.desc: Nomads of the Burning Sands, who know every well, every buried city and every lie the dunes tell.
traits: +2 to Survival to find water, shade and a safe road in the desert.
You must shelter any guest and avenge any slain one. Accept the cost.
+2 to Read People to spot riders, ambushes and liars in open country.
Omens and ill signs sway you. Accept the delay or the detour.
+2 to Riding on camels and across sand.
Your tribe's honor is yours. Accept the duty when it calls.

origins.name: Islander
origins.desc: From the Shattered Isles of the south: corsairs, pearl-divers and sea-witches' children.
traits: +2 to Athletics to swim, dive and hold your breath.
Land makes you restless. Accept the risk to get back aboard.
+2 to Athletics to climb, balance and swing.
You keep the brotherhood's code. Accept the cost of keeping it.
+2 to Sailing to read weather, tides and currents.
Money runs through your fingers. Accept being broke at the wrong moment.

origins.name: Ashborn
origins.desc: Grey-skinned descendants of the empire's sorcery-bred slave legions. The empire is gone; the brand remains.
core: Fire-blooded: fire and heat mark one fewer box on you (minimum 0).
traits: +2 to Melee when fighting shoulder to shoulder with an ally.
The empire's brand still marks you. Accept the contempt, or an old master's claim.
+2 to Body rolls to endure heat, thirst, poison or pain.
Grey skin draws stares and stones. Accept the hostility.
+2 to Leadership with soldiers, slaves and the desperate.
Commands in the old tongue still grip you. Roll Will or obey; accept the consequence.

origins.name: Deepkin
origins.desc: Pale folk from the cities beneath the mountains, who trade with the surface and fear what lies deeper.
core: Darksight: you see in darkness as if by dim light.
Sun-shy: in bright sunlight, −1 to Agility and its skills.
traits: +2 to Investigation to find hidden doors, traps and passages underground.
Daylight blinds you at the worst moment. Accept the stumble.
+2 to Stealth underground and in darkness.
Surface folk find you uncanny. Accept the suspicion.
+2 to Craft with metal and stone.
You can't leave fine metalwork behind. Accept the weight, or the risk.

origins.name: Witch-blooded
origins.desc: Human, with old sorcery in the veins: a witch grandmother, a sorcerer's bastard, or a pact made before you were born.
core: To cast cantrips you need a casting calling (Sorcerer or Witch), Gifted, or The Old Blood.
traits: You are Gifted: you can learn cantrips and work rituals (see Sorcery).
Animals shy and the pious cross themselves. Accept the suspicion, or the mob.
+2 to Sorcery to sense curses, spirits and hostile magic nearby.
The dead find you and want things. Accept their demands.
+2 to Sorcery to Hex someone who has wronged you.
You never forgive a slight. Accept the trouble a grudge brings.

origins.name: Giant-blooded
origins.desc: Seven feet and more, with a giant somewhere in the family tree. Strong, feared, and always too big for the door.
core: Huge: your fists and kicks mark 2 boxes. Armor, saddles and doorways must be made for you.
traits: +2 to Athletics to lift, break, push or throw.
You don't fit. Accept the broken chair, the stuck tunnel or the frightened crowd.
Once per scene, a hit that would mark 1 box marks none.
Children run and guards draw swords. Accept the trouble.
+2 to Leadership to rally allies or frighten enemies in battle.
Small folk have tricked you before. Accept the cost of refusing help.

origins.name: Serpent-kin
origins.desc: Last heirs of the serpent empire that ruled before humans. Scaled, cold-eyed, venomous, and distrusted everywhere.
core: Cold blood: in freezing cold, −1 to all rolls.
Venom: your bite marks 1 box and poisons (Body roll or Reeling).
traits: +2 to Brawling with your bite; on a hit the target rolls Body or is Reeling.
Every human remembers the serpent kings. Accept the hatred.
+2 to Persuasion to charm someone who meets your eyes.
Warmth and grief are strange to you. Accept the offense it gives.
You are Gifted: you can learn cantrips and work rituals (see Sorcery).
You seek the serpent empire's relics. Accept the risk to claim one.

origins.name: Demon-marked
origins.desc: Born of, bargained with, or claimed by the infernal: horns, burning eyes or a shadow that moves on its own.
core: Infernal: fire marks one fewer box on you; holy rites and true names mark one extra.
Marked: your sign is hard to hide.
traits: You are Gifted: you can learn cantrips and work rituals (see Sorcery).
Your demon parent or patron wants something. Accept its demand.
+2 to Sorcery with fire; your Witchfire marks 2 boxes.
Priests and the pious see a devil. Accept their wrath.
+2 to Deception to tempt someone toward greed, lust or betrayal.
Your own appetites run hot. Accept the indulgence.

origins.name: Skinchanger
origins.desc: Beast-cursed: wolf, bear or great cat. You pass for human until fury or the moon lets the beast out.
core: Cold iron: weapons of cold iron mark one extra box on you in beast form.
The moon: on the full moon, a Will roll at −2 or the beast takes you for the night.

traits: Beast-quick: run and leap like an animal
drawbacks: Can't speak, cast or use tools

traits: +2 to Tracking by scent, in either form.
When blood is spilled, the beast wants out. Roll Will or change; accept the cost.
+2 to Brawling or Melee against a target an ally attacked this round.
Walls and chains drive you mad. Accept the risk to get out.
Once a day, between scenes, clear one injury box (not while Dying).
The full moon always comes at the worst time. Accept the changed plans.

origins.name: Godblooded
origins.desc: Descended from a god who died when the Crown shattered. Miracles follow you, and so do those who want the god's last spark.
core: Miracle: once per venture, the GM grants a small impossible thing: a door opens, a wound closes, a storm turns.
Hunted: rival priests and demons know you on sight.
traits: You are Gifted: you can learn cantrips and work rituals (see Sorcery).
Your god's purpose comes first. Accept the sign that sends you elsewhere.
+2 to Leadership with crowds and the faithful.
Fanatics follow you. Accept their zeal and its consequences.
+2 to Will to resist sorcery, possession and fear.
Servants of rival gods hunt you. Accept the ambush.

origins.name: Undying
origins.desc: A sorcerer who cheated death. Your heart no longer beats; your soul waits in a hidden phylactery.
core: Deathless: you don't age or breathe; Healing can't mend you. Draining life can: Sorcery against a victim's Body; on a success you clear a box and they mark one.
Hunger (dark campaign): each week you must drain a living soul, or mark a box of Corruption.
Phylactery: you truly die only if your hidden phylactery is destroyed; otherwise you return within a month.
traits: You are Gifted: you can learn cantrips and work rituals (see Sorcery). +2 to Sorcery for rituals of death.
The living smell of warmth. Roll Will or feed; accept the cost.
+2 to Leadership and Sorcery to frighten the living.
Someone is near your phylactery's hiding place. Accept the detour.
+2 to Lore about the old empire and its sorcerers.
Rivals from your first life still live, or don't. Accept their return.

allegiances: guild
The Thieves' Guild
Once per venture, a fence, a safehouse or a rumor from the streets.
Duty: the guild takes its cut, and sends you its jobs.
ironco
The Iron Company
Once per venture, a squad of soldiers, arms or a warhorse.
Duty: the company's contracts come first.
cult
The Cult of the Burning God
Once per venture, shelter, healing or a handful of zealots.
Duty: hunt sorcerers and heretics when the cult demands it.
prince
A Sorcerer-Prince
Once per venture, gold, a spell worked on your behalf, or a forbidden book.
Duty: fetch what the prince desires, and ask no questions.
merchants
The Merchant Princes
Once per venture, passage on a ship or caravan, coin, or an introduction.
Duty: protect their trade, and their secrets.
clan
A Northern Clan
Once per venture, warriors, a longship or a place in the hall.
Duty: the clan's feuds are yours.
reasons: Gold
Gold, and plenty of it. Everything else follows.
Vengeance
Someone took everything from me. I mean to take it back, in blood.
Glory
I want my name in the songs when I'm dust.
Freedom
No master, no chains, no one to answer to.
The Crown
Find a shard of the Crown, and the world bends to the one who holds it.
Knowledge
The old empire's secrets are out there. I will read them.
Faith
My god is dying. Someone has to keep the flame.
Survival
Every day alive is a victory. I mean to have more of them.
Redemption
I did terrible things. I mean to balance the scales.
Thrill
Danger is the only thing that makes me feel alive.
connections: Shared a cell
We were chained in the same slave pit and broke out together.
They saved my life
They pulled me from the sea, or the sands, or a burning city.
I saved theirs
I cut them down from the gallows, and they haven't forgotten it.
Old comrades
We fought in the same company and still watch each other's backs.
Rivals
We always want the same treasure, the same title or the same lover.
Same homeland
We grew up in the same place and know each other's families.
An unpaid debt
I owe them money, or a favor, and I haven't paid it yet.
A shared secret
We know what really happened in the tomb. No one else does.
Mentor
They taught me to fight, steal or cast. I'm still learning.
Bound by an oath
We swore an oath together before a god, or a demon.
advantages: Ignore the −1 for your first injury box.
+2 to Melee with one chosen kind of weapon.
Your shield also gives an ally beside you +1 Dodge.
Once per scene, +2 to Melee and Brawling until the fight ends; you can't retreat or Dodge.
Reload a firearm in one action instead of a full round; it misfires only on a natural 18.
+2 to Thievery to pick pockets and palm objects.
+2 to Thievery and Craft against locks and traps.
+2 to Persuasion when bargaining or haggling.
+2 to Deception when telling a single, specific lie.
+2 to Read People to spot lies and ambushes.
+2 to Survival in desert and wasteland; you never get lost there.
+2 to Sailing, and no penalty for fighting on a pitching deck.
+2 to Riding, and no penalty for fighting from the saddle.
+2 to Lore about ruins, old empires and monsters.
+2 to Healing with herbs; brew a remedy overnight without a satchel.
You can learn cantrips and work rituals (see Sorcery).
Once per scene, mark an injury box instead of a box of Corruption.
+2 to Will to resist sorcery, fear and charm.
+2 to Stealth in darkness or crowds.
Once per venture, a deal, a price or a reward goes your way.
+2 to Lore about a creature you face, and +1 to hit it once you know its weakness.
complications: You can't walk away from treasure. Accept the risk to grab it.
A clan or house wants you dead. Accept the ambush or the challenge.
There's a price on your head in one of the Crown's cities. Accept the hunters it brings.
You swore a vow you must keep, whatever it costs. Accept the cost.
A sorcerer will ask a favor, and you can't refuse. Accept the errand.
Something infernal follows you. Accept its interference.
Your weapon thirsts and must taste blood. Accept the fight it wants.
Beauty and passion tempt you at the worst moments. Accept the distraction.
Wine, or the lotus-dream. Accept the craving when it bites.
Insults are answered with steel. Accept the brawl.
You're exiled from your people. Accept their scorn, or their hunters.
A massacre, a betrayal, a dead love. Accept the memory's grip.
You won't rest until they're dead. Accept the detour toward them.
You won't back down or ask for help. Accept the consequence.
You charge first and think later. Accept the danger it puts you in.
You refuse a spell's aid and fear those who cast. Accept the cost of refusing.
You know something that could topple a throne. Accept the danger of keeping it.
Someone is always a step ahead or behind you. Accept their interference.
The sorcery is taking you. Accept the urge, the sign or the whisper.

The party agrees to leave the treasure
A merchant offers more than the job pays
feud: A stranger wears your enemies' colors
Word reaches you of a kinsman's death
A challenge is shouted across a crowded hall
wanted: Wanted posters in the market square
A guard looks twice at your face
A bounty hunter takes the next room
oath: Keeping the vow means abandoning the plan
Someone you swore to protect is in danger
Breaking the oath would be easy and profitable
sorcdebt: A raven arrives with a sealed message
The sorcerer's mark burns on your skin
The errand leads exactly where you don't want to go
demon: Sulphur in the air and dead birds
Someone speaks with a voice not their own
A bargain is offered when things are darkest
blade: A fight ends without blood drawn
The blade whispers in the night
Someone tries to take the blade from you
lust: A beautiful stranger with a dangerous lover
A seduction offered as a trap
Passion at the moment you should be on watch
cup: A lotus den on the way to the job
fuse: An insult to your name or your people
Someone laughs at you in a crowded room
A guard shoves you once too often
outcast: Your people's camp lies on the road
Your people need help and won't ask
haunted: A place that looks like the one where it happened
Someone repeats the last words you heard
A face from the past in a crowd
vengeance: News of where your enemy is
A choice between the job and the hunt
proud: Someone questions your strength or skill
Help is offered in front of others
A task is beyond you, and you know it
reckless: A closed door in a dangerous place
The cautious plan takes too long
distrust: A friend offers a healing spell
The only way through is magic
secret: A powerful figure asks what you know
The secret could save a friend if told
corrupted: Power is offered at the moment of need
The sign on your skin flares in public

equipment: The common weapon of the Crownlands. Hits mark 2 boxes.
Two hands. Hits mark 2 boxes, and a hit by 5 or more leaves the target Dying.
Reach in a crowd or a shield-wall. Hits mark 2 boxes.
Hidden in a boot or a sleeve. Hits mark 1 box.
Twenty arrows. Hits mark 2 boxes. Long range.
Twelve bolts; reloading takes an action. +2 to hit at Close range. Hits mark 2 boxes. Medium range.
One shot; reloading takes a full round. Hits mark 2 boxes. Rain ruins the powder. Close range.
One shot; reloading takes a full round. Hits mark 3 boxes and leave the target Dying; misfires on a natural 17–18. Rain ruins the powder. Short range.
Three, thrown with Athletics: 1 box to everyone nearby, 3 and Dying at the center. Close range (thrown).
Hits of 2 or more boxes mark one fewer, once per fight. −1 to Stealth and Athletics for swimming.
+1 Dodge against attacks you can see, and +1 to Block.
Light in the tombs, and fire when you need it.
Picks, files and a dark lantern. Needed for most Thievery against locks.
Herbs, needles and bandages. Needed to stabilize a patient and give field treatment.
Powders, flasks and a small furnace. Needed for most alchemy and to make bombs.
A staff, a skull, a holy symbol or a grimoire. Needed for rituals.
Carries you across the wilds. Riding in a chase needs one.
Charts, a spyglass and a sailor's kit.

tracks.name: Infamy
effects: Wanted posters: −2 to Persuasion with the watch

tracks.name: Doom
effects: Ill omens: ravens, black cats, bad dreams
A sorcerer scries you: −2 to Stealth against magic
It comes for you: start a clock

tracks.name: Debt
effects: Your gear or mounts are seized
A creditor names the price: a job you can't refuse

tracks.name: Hunger
effects: Hungry: −1 to all rolls on the road
Collapse: find food today or someone dies

spells.note: Your Sorcery sets your Seal: the First at Trained (no Boosts), the Second at Specialty (1 Boost), the Third at Expert (2 Boosts). Casting takes an action and a Sorcery roll, −1 for each Boost you spend; the target resists with Will where it makes sense. A failed cast marks a box of Corruption; a natural 18 marks two.
list: A ranged attack with Sorcery; marks 2 boxes. Dodge applies.
Light, or set something burning: 1 box a round in the flames.
Attacks against one ally are at −2 for the scene.
The target is at −2 on all rolls for the scene (Will resists).
Presence contest: the target treats you as a friend for the scene.
The target rolls Will or flees or freezes.
The target rolls Will or sleeps; minor opponents just drop.
Clear one injury box, once per wound.
Speak with an animal, and command it for a scene.
See magic, curses, spirits and disguised monsters.
Break a lock, chain, blade or door.
+3 to Stealth for the scene; you're hard to notice.

personalTrack.name: Corruption
effects: Marked: a visible sign of sorcery
Tainted: −2 to Persuasion with the pious
Twisted: the GM can trigger a madness or compulsion
Lost: the power claims you; only a great rite can bring you back

quickRef: Fists, daggers, slings: 1 box. Swords, axes, bows, crossbows, pistols, claws: 2. Arquebus: 3 and Dying. Greatweapon hit by 5+: Dying.
Quiver 20, bolts 12, pistol and arquebus 1 shot. Crossbow reload: an action; firearms: a full round. Natural 18: string snaps or powder fails.

Cantrips: an action and a Sorcery roll; known Trained 2, Specialty 3, Expert 4. Seals: Specialty 1 Boost, Expert 2 (−1 each to the roll). Rituals: 2-, 4- or 6-segment clock. Talismans: 2, 3, 4. Enchantments: a ritual worked into an item, +1 segment to last a day, +2 a moon; they share the talisman limit.
Failed cast: 1 box; natural 18: 2; finishing a Major ritual: 1. Marked, Tainted, Twisted, Lost. A cleansing rite or pilgrimage clears one.

example.name: Kara of the Long Winter
example.role: Came south on a longship with nine brothers. She is the only one who came back from the Tomb of Ashes.
example.reason: Someone took everything from me. I mean to take it back, in blood.
example.connection: Mira Saltwind pulled her out of the sea after the longship burned; Kara owes her a life.

comp.trigger: News of where your enemy is

pregens.name: Vessa Thorn
pregens.role: The best climber in the Gilded Cities, who stole a jewel from a sorcerer-prince and is only now learning it's a shard of the Crown.
pregens.reason: Gold, and plenty of it. Everything else follows.
pregens.connection: Cinder was paid to kill her and didn't. Neither of them has said why.

comp.trigger: A powerful figure asks what you know

pregens.contact: Old Marrow, a fence in the Gilded Cities who buys anything and asks nothing

pregens.name: Ithrann
pregens.role: Keeper of a drowned serpent temple's memory, searching the human kingdoms for its lost library.
pregens.reason: The old empire's secrets are out there. I will read them.
pregens.connection: Oren Sael shelters Ithrann at his shrine when no inn will take a serpent-kin.

pregens.name: Nyx
pregens.role: Run out of her village with stones and torches; sells cures and curses to whoever pays.
pregens.reason: Every day alive is a victory. I mean to have more of them.
pregens.connection: Gorrum carried her out of the burning village. He says he was just passing.

comp.trigger: A raven arrives with a sealed message

pregens.name: Gorrum Ironjaw
pregens.role: Twenty years with the Iron Company, a wheel-lock pistol he calls Thunder, and a soft spot for strays.
pregens.reason: I did terrible things. I mean to balance the scales.
pregens.connection: Nyx is the stray he carried out of the fire. He'd die before he'd say he cares.

pregens.name: Mira Saltwind
pregens.role: Captain of the Kestrel until a sea-witch sank her. She kept her mother's arquebus and her crew's debts.
pregens.reason: Someone took everything from me. I mean to take it back, in blood.
pregens.connection: Kara of the Long Winter owes her a life, and Mira means to collect.

comp.trigger: News of where your enemy is

pregens.name: Cinder
pregens.rank: Former blade of the Ash Guild
pregens.role: Made by the Ash Guild into its best knife; ran the night they ordered a child's death.
pregens.reason: No master, no chains, no one to answer to.

magic.steps: the First Seal at Trained, the Second at Specialty, the Third at Expert
dials: Sword and sorcery: magic is power, and power has a price.
Sorcerers, Witches, the Gifted and the gifted origins. Known: Trained 2, Specialty 3, Expert 4.
Every cantrip holds three Seals, each hiding a deeper power. Sorcery breaks them: the First at Trained, the Second (1 Boost) at Specialty, the Third (2 Boosts) at Expert.
Anyone with Sorcery: ten minutes a roll, an hour for great workings. Priests work rites the same way with Lore.
A ritual bound into a bone, a ring or a knotted cord, released by breaking it.
A ritual worked into an object, lasting a scene, a day (+1 segment), a moon (+2) or until broken (Major only). Talismans and enchantments share one limit: Trained 2, Specialty 3, Expert 4.
Corruption: a failed cantrip marks 1, a natural 18 marks 2, and finishing a Major ritual marks 1, whatever the roll.

help.step: Every cantrip holds three Seals, each hiding a deeper power. Your Sorcery breaks them: the First Seal at Trained, the Second at Specialty, the Third at Expert.
help.price: Finishing a Major ritual marks 1 Corruption too, whatever the roll. A cleansing rite or a pilgrimage between ventures clears a box.
help.charms: Talismans and enchantments share one limit: as many as your Sorcery training allows, Trained 2, Specialty 3, Expert 4. An enchantment is a ritual worked into an object that lasts (a scene, a day, a moon, or until broken) rather than being spent.

extraEdges: Start each venture with one ready talisman holding a Minor ritual agreed with the GM. Anyone can break it; it's renewed between ventures and doesn't count against a talisman limit.

extraEdges.placeholder: e.g. A knotted cord against poison, from my grandmother

extraEdges: One item carries a lasting Significant enchantment: +2 to one use, or its hits mark one more box, or it turns one hit a fight. Sight sees it; Shatter's Third Seal or a rite of unbinding can break it.

extraEdges.label: Your enchanted heirloom

ward.name: Enchantment: turns one hit a fight
ward.text: A lasting Significant enchantment: once per fight, a hit of 2 or more boxes marks one fewer.

protection.name: Shield
protection.text: +1 Dodge against attacks you can see, and +1 to Block.

protection.name: Mail shirt
protection.text: Hits of 2 or more boxes mark one fewer, once per fight. −1 to Stealth and Athletics for swimming.

table.name: Lost limb
table.text: A hand, an arm or a leg is gone for good; the GM says which. −4 to tasks that need it, or impossible. Dying unless someone stops the bleeding.

table.name: Lost eye or scarred face
table.text: An eye is gone or the face is ruined: −2 to Marksmanship and spotting things, or to winning strangers over; the GM says which.

table.name: Broken bone
table.text: The limb is useless until it's set with proper care.

table.name: Concussion
table.text: Reeling, and −2 to thinking tasks for the scene.

table.name: Internal injury
table.text: Dying even with boxes to spare; it needs a master healer or a temple's surgeons.

{name} drops like a sack of grain.

{name} takes a bolt through the throat and goes down choking.

spell: Witchfire takes {name}, and what's left smokes.
{name}'s blood boils in their veins; they fall without a sound.
The spell turns {name} to ash from the hands up.

gmGuide.title: The Shattered Crown GM's Guide
gmGuide.subtitle: Running sword and sorcery: ventures, threats and the GM's tools
gmGuide.intro: This book is for whoever runs the game, and anyone can read it. It gathers what the GM reaches for at the table: venture seeds, the threats with their numbers, and how to use the GM view's battle map and Encounter panel. The rules themselves are in the **Players' Guide**; this book builds on them.
gmGuide.playersNote: The material for running the game (venture seeds, the threats, and the GM's tools) is in a companion book, the **GM's Guide**.
